findings.title: group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer instead of a User object
findings.body: In `remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` is called where `user_id` is an integer (from `params.require(:user_id).to_i`). ActiveRecord's `CollectionProxy#delete` expects record objects, not IDs. This call will silently fail to remove the user from the group. It should be something like `group.users.where(id: user_id).delete_all` or find the user first and then delete the object.

findings.title: Unclosed {{each}} block causes broken template
findings.body: The `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` block on line 21 is never closed with `{{/each}}`. The `` on line 22 closes the parent div immediately after opening the each block, meaning member items will never render and the template will likely throw a Handlebars compilation error or produce malformed HTML.

findings.title: No upper bound on limit parameter allows unbounded queries
findings.body: The `members` action accepts `params[:limit]` with no maximum cap: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`. A client can pass an arbitrarily large value (e.g., limit=999999) to force the server to load and serialize the entire group membership in a single query, potentially causing memory exhaustion or denial of service for large groups. A reasonable upper bound should be enforced.

findings.title: remove_member test uses wrong HTTP method (:put instead of :delete)
findings.body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` but the route defines `remove_member` as a DELETE endpoint (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`). While controller specs can invoke actions directly regardless of HTTP verb, this inconsistency with the other remove_member test on line 125 (which correctly uses `:delete`) suggests a copy-paste error and means the test doesn't verify the actual request path a client would use.

findings.title: Missing semicolon after addMembers promise chain
findings.body: The `addMembers` method's `.then()` call on line 59 is missing a trailing semicolon. While JavaScript's ASI will likely handle this in most cases, it is inconsistent with the `removeMember` method (line 48) which does have a semicolon, and could cause subtle issues with certain minifiers or if code is later appended on the next line.
